refreshes.scope: Retention measurement and programme under PenniLogic/docs#8: the activation funnel and week-one and week-four cohorts (android#7), the retention programme with milestones, digests, dormancy re-engagement and its kill criterion (android#38), server-side experiment assignment and exposure logging (api#63), the analytics ingestion endpoint, pipeline and team dashboard (api#82, created on 2026-09-30 from finding E07-F05 and reconciled into this refresh the same day), the debt-first concept test (docs#53, Sprint 01) and moderated usability of the onboarding and permission prototype (docs#54). The threat surface is the analytics pipeline (event payloads, pseudonymous identifiers, opt-out, retention and erasure of events and exposure rows, the dashboard the team reads), experiment assignment and exposure integrity, retention messaging that surfaces debt status outside the app and transits the push provider, the age gate every flow must respect, and the participants of the two studies. The epic's own exit criteria already forbid financial values in any analytics payload; this refresh records the controls that make that provable and the gaps around them.

categories.analysis: Analytics identities are pseudonymous, so spoofing here means a client claiming another identity's events or a treatment it was not assigned. Server-side assignment and server-stamped exposure logging (E07-F04) are the control; a client-chosen identifier or self-reported assignment would let one device manufacture another cohort's behaviour.
evidence: architecture/02-security-architecture.md#8-privacy-engineering: analytics identifiers are a keyed hash of the user identifier, unlinkable without the pepper

categories.analysis: The retention signal decides whether the product continues, so the integrity of events, assignments and cohorts is the asset. Two gaps: assignment and exposure must be server-side and written only by the server, with no update or delete path outside the erasure job (E07-F04), and event ingestion, the pipeline and the dashboard the team reads had no owning ticket for schema validation, rate limits and deduplication when this refresh was first performed, so forged or inflated events from a rooted device or a script would be counted (E07-F05, since handed to api#82 and reconciled with its body).

Opt-out must be provable and effective: a user who opted out and later sees their behaviour in a cohort has a valid dispute, and the product must be able to show which purpose entry and consent version governed analytics and experimentation at the time. The control is a server-side record in the consent ledger (compliance O-1, api#24) that ingestion, assignment and exposure logging consult, not a client flag alone (E07-F03).
evidence: PenniLogic/api#24: consent ledger, purpose registry and data-principal rights
compliance/01-regulatory-landscape.md obligation O-16: analytics opt-out surface

categories.analysis: Events and exposure rows are pseudonymous personal data: the server holds the pepper and can re-identify, so they need a published retention period and an erasure path, not only an allowlist (E07-F03, E07-F05). Four channels leak debt status. Event payloads: the exit criterion forbids financial values, but derived values such as payoff horizon, debt count or milestone are quasi-financial and need coarsening, and the allowlist needs a test rather than a code review (E07-F01). Retention messages: a digest or dormancy nudge puts a balance or a debt-free date on a lock screen, an e-mail preview or a widget where a household member reads it, and every message transits the push or e-mail provider, a processor that must appear in the component and SDK inventory (O-7) and receive allowlisted text only (E07-F02). Children: the compliance record restricts the product to adults and behavioural monitoring of a child is prohibited, yet nothing conditions instrumentation, assignment or messaging on the age gate (E07-F07). Study participants: the concept test and usability sessions gather personal financial disclosures under the research evidence system, including household co-participants (E07-F06). Dashboards over small cohorts are part of the pipeline finding (E07-F05).
evidence: PenniLogic/docs#8 exit criteria: zero financial values in any analytics payload, verified by inspecting captured events
PenniLogic/android#16: automated privacy traffic inspection on every release candidate (E25)
compliance/01-regulatory-landscape.md obligations O-4 (retention and crypto-erasure), O-6 (age gate), O-7 (processor and SDK inventory)

categories.analysis: An event flood from one device or script inflates ingestion cost and buries real signal; without per-device rate limits and deduplication in the pipeline the same gap as E07-F05 applies.

No privileged operation is introduced: analytics events are write-only from the client, assignment is read-only for the client, and access to aggregate views belongs to the admin console (E13, admin#7), which its own refresh reviews.
No payment or entitlement path is touched. Retention messaging about plans is designed in docs#98 (E35) and billing itself in E14.

No entitlement state is read or written; experiment assignment is not an entitlement and must not gate paid features (a treatment that unlocks a paid feature would be an entitlement path and a scope_changed trigger for this record).

No model, gateway or provider key is used; digests and milestones are template-driven. Generating digest text with a model would be a scope_changed trigger and would bring prompt injection through merchant names into scope.
The clients are native applications posting to first-party endpoints; no browser session is exposed and no supplied URL is fetched. Forged event posts are a tampering concern (E07-F05).
No model reads untrusted content in this epic; see the ai_service_compromise note on template-driven digests.
No shared ledger or settlement is involved; retention events about split features, when E15 exists, must follow the same allowlist as every other event.

The epic introduces no operator identity. Whoever administers the analytics dashboard is part of the pipeline finding (E07-F05, api#82) and, once the dashboard exists, of the admin console's operator model (E13).

findings.title: The event allowlist must be a tested schema and must coarsen derived debt values
findings.attack_path: An event carries an amount, balance, merchant name, account reference or a precise derived value such as a payoff date or debt count; it leaves the device and is stored in the analytics pipeline, where it re-identifies financial status even though no raw amount was sent.
findings.recommended_control: An allowlisted event schema enforced by a unit test that fails on any unknown property; derived values emitted only as coarse bands; identifiers as a keyed hash with a server-held pepper; captured release-candidate traffic inspected against the same schema (android#16).

findings.title: Digests, milestones and dormancy nudges can expose debt status outside the app
findings.attack_path: A progress digest, milestone or re-engagement message shows a balance, a debt-free date or the word debt on a lock screen, in an e-mail subject or preview, or in a widget, where a family member, colleague or abuser reads it; the same text transits the push or e-mail provider, so a processor outside the component and SDK inventory receives debt status.
findings.recommended_control: Message content chosen server-side from an allowlist with no financial values or debt words in any surface shown outside the unlocked app; privacy mode honoured; user-controlled channel and content preferences; the push and e-mail providers recorded as processors in the component and SDK inventory (compliance O-7, android#18) and sent token or address plus allowlisted text only; the retention programme's kill criterion measured without exposing the value that triggered the message.

findings.title: Analytics opt-out, purpose and consent version must be recorded and enforced server-side, with a retention period and an erasure path for events and exposure rows
findings.attack_path: A user opts out on one device; the flag lives only in that client, a second device or a reinstall keeps reporting, and exposure logging continues on the server, so the user's dispute is valid and the product cannot show when opt-out took effect, which purpose entry and consent version governed the processing, or that an erasure request reached the pseudonymous rows the server can still re-identify.
findings.recommended_control: Opt-out written to the consent ledger with a timestamp under a registered purpose entry for analytics and experimentation that names its consent version (O-1); ingestion, assignment and exposure logging consult it on every request and stop; clients treat the server state as authoritative; a published retention period for events and exposure rows and an erasure job that deletes a subject's rows by pseudonymous identifier (O-2, O-4), shared with api#82; tests prove an opted-out identity produces no rows and an erased identity has none left.

findings.title: Experiment assignment and exposure must be server-side, with no write path but the server's and no delete path but the erasure job
findings.attack_path: A client reports its own treatment or posts exposure events for a treatment it never saw; a rooted device or script shifts cohort behaviour and the holdout comparison that drives the kill decision; or an operator edits or drops rows to change the result.
findings.recommended_control: Deterministic server-side assignment returned to the client, exposure rows written by the server with its own timestamp, no client-supplied assignment or exposure accepted, no update path, and no delete path outside the erasure job that api#82 and E07-F03 define, so integrity for the experiment's life and erasure for the data subject are both satisfied.

findings.title: Event ingestion, the pipeline and the team dashboard had no owning ticket
findings.attack_path: Forged, replayed or flooded events from a rooted device or a script are accepted without schema validation, per-device rate limits or deduplication; the retention signal that decides whether the debt-first wedge continues is corrupted, ingestion cost rises, and a dashboard over a small cohort re-identifies users.
findings.recommended_control: An owning ticket for the ingestion endpoint and pipeline: schema validation against the E07-F01 allowlist, per-identity rate limits and deduplication, an append-only store with a published retention period and a deletion path tied to erasure requests (no update or delete outside the erasure job), acceptance conditioned on the server-side opt-out state and the age gate, a dashboard with cohort minimums and a named access list, and no third-party analytics SDK on the client.

findings.title: Concept-test and usability participants fall under the research evidence system
findings.attack_path: Recordings and notes from the debt-first concept test or the onboarding usability sessions, which include personal debt disclosures, are stored or quoted outside the participant-data rules because the studies sit in this epic rather than in E33; both members of a household are recruited through one channel or cross-referenced in the notes, so one learns the other's participation; a minor is interviewed about household debt.
findings.recommended_control: Both studies run under the participant evidence system: classification, storage and access list, consent and withdrawal records, pseudonymised quotes, retention and erasure, no raw artifact in a repository, issue or prompt, separate recruitment channels and sessions for household members with no cross-reference in the evidence system, and an age screen excluding anyone under 18 (the same controls as E33-F01, E33-F02 and E33-F03).

findings.title: Instrumentation, experiment assignment and retention messaging are not conditioned on the age gate
findings.attack_path: An account that has not passed, or has failed, the pre-onboarding age gate still emits analytics events, is assigned to an experiment and receives digests and dormancy nudges; the product performs behavioural monitoring of a child, which the compliance record's adults-only position and the children's-data obligation forbid.
findings.recommended_control: Every event, assignment, exposure row and retention message is gated server-side on an age-gate-passed state recorded with the consent ledger entry (O-6, android#17); the ingestion endpoint (api#82) refuses events for an identity without it, and the assignment service (api#63), the messaging outbox (api#56) and the retention programme (android#38) apply the same state; a test proves an account below the gate produces no event, no exposure row and no message.
